title: Into the Heart of Darkroot Forest: The Quest for the Tunnel of Doom
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pRB23hC8dZY

For a Solo RPG Friday with a difference, Daniel (@dungeondive) leaves the hobby room behind and heads out on foot into "Dark Root Forest" in search of the legendary Tunnel of Doom — a real-world, make-believe quest narrated in character.

Along the way he recalls the solo expeditions he planned as a kid: packing snacks the night before and playing out quests in the undeveloped high desert near Magic Mountain, on land Disney used for westerns, with a stick for a broadsword and a well-practised Conan twirl. The forest itself becomes the adventure, with long stretches of music and footage as he points out a mossy shrine, a hermit's hut best avoided and the Swamps of Despair.

The heart of the video is a reflection on why he has always gravitated to playing alone. In solo play he never had to explain his world's rules — that in his G.I. Joe, Storm Shadow never joined Cobra — and as an adult he controls the tone, humour, horror and action without worrying whether anyone else is having fun. He wonders whether other solo gamers were the same as children.

He reaches the tunnel, and leaves what lies beyond it for another day.

----

Daniel asks it directly: did you gravitate to playing alone as a kid, and do you think that's why solo gaming appeals to you now?
